newsitem.title: UK: Dtd Brent still in slump, Nigerian slides.
newsitem.headline: Dtd Brent still in slump, Nigerian slides.

text.p: Heavy discounts for North Sea marker Dated Brent showed no sign of reviving on Wednesday morning.

Several Brents remain available with a major after two sales at Dec -45 and -48 cents on Tuesday. Lower CFD offers by the same company for next weeks' Brent dates ignited speculation that Dated values could drop lower.
A trader holding four cargoes was thought likely to ship the crude out of Europe.
Three more Brents were nominated down paper chains on Wednesday.

Most other North Sea grades were still showing for November with third decade Statfjord barely touched yet. Oseberg was in shorter supply after two prompt cargoes moved on Tuesday at lower values of Brent +15 cents.
Intermonth spreads were slightly narrower at +32 cents for Dec/Jan Brent.
Nigerian spot crude values looked increasingly vulnerable on Wednesday as an overhang of remaining November material was supplemented by two late spot cargoes.
Dealers said an impossible spot arbitrage to the U.S. had left several cargoes without homes.
Qua Iboe headed toward a sub-Dated Brent +40 cent value for November loaders after trades at about +42 earlier this week into Indonesia and Dakar.
An extra cargo each of Qua Iboe and Escravos were added to the November market after two local Nigerian companies decided at the last minute not to sell the crude in a falling market.
Two Qua Iboes set to load on a VLCC in the Nov 10-13 period and two Escravos for mid-to-end month were looking for homes.
A Nov 27-29 Brass River also remained unsold. Some 400,000 barrels of million-barrel Forcados/Brass mix also was expected to look for a spot buyer.
